description.value:
Frequency at will

You and your Feral Bond each Stride up to your Speed + 10 feet, leaving no trail and triggering no reactions (including attacks of opportunity) for this movement.

cinderfall.incomplete: Hands the actor a new, distinct movement action (extended Stride + reaction immunity) — bucket 3 territory regardless of "at will" framing (see P8/P9: even real pf2e's own bespoke movement/Strike actions need hardcoded system support beyond system.rules). Applying the same benefit to the Feral Bond simultaneously is also cross-creature. This hands the actor a wholly new usable action/reaction. Confirmed absent per two direct spot checks: Fighter's Double Slice only rule-encodes its minor non-agile penalty -- the actual "resolve two Strikes as one attack, combine damage" behavior is hardcoded PF2e system logic. Fighter's Reactive Strike is granted via a bare GrantItem whose trigger is likewise hardcoded system behavior tied to one specific compendium action UUID, not a generic rule-element hook. Any Waywarden card proposing an equivalent bespoke Strike-triggering or multi-Strike-resolving action inherits the same gap. This effect buffs, protects, or grants actions to the Feral Bond (the companion beast) from the holder's own card. No rule-element selector in pf2e-source lets one actor's item grant a stat bonus, temp HP, an extra action, or a shared sense to a different actor's sheet -- confirmed by spot-checking real pf2e's own fully-built Animal Companion subsystem (Ranger/Druid), where virtually every companion-buff/companion-action-economy feat ships with rules: [] too.
